verdicts.ambition_why: Collapsing three drifting encodings of the AGENTS.md authority rule into one judge, so that the verifier a judge runs is as strict as the gauntlet, is the principal-engineer move for the 'provable' claim.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every cited line reads as claimed, including the lax branches, the query-strip divergence and owner_saw skipping voids.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-5 are each red today and each names one branch, and the agreement property (case 8) catches any divergence; the v1 carve-out is the one under-specified edge.
verdicts.revision: State that the v1 Human exemption applies only to verify_bundle's 'authority' check, and that safety::unlawful keeps demanding an earlier owner.decision for Human on every format. Add the case: v1 bundle with a Human capture and no owner.decision -> safety::unlawful is Some (as today) while verify_bundle 'authority' ok=true. As written, 'judge = conjunction of both rules' plus 'owner.decision demand only on v2' would quietly loosen the safety predicate on v1 files once unlawful becomes a thin wrapper over judge.
verdicts.builder_notes: The safety.rs:424-427 test asserts that a query'd capture is 'capture' and must be reversed (declared). The gauntlet.rs mutation tests (STATUS 1767) must pass unchanged. Keep /v1/billing/subscriptions/{id}/capture (table-paypal secondary.rs:356) classified the same in both readers. Every proof_tests/glass_tests/ladder_tests/safety_tests export must still read VERIFIED. No Rust IPC/authority/bindings/PINNED_MANIFEST change; the in-app proof_check verdict changes only for bundles that the safety predicate already flags.

verdicts.ambition_why: Removing the hidden O(N) pass behind every read attacks the root multiplier of the open scale finding without touching IPC; a principal engineer would pick that over client workarounds.
verdicts.grounding_why: The loop shape, the vault read counts and the single-connection ledger all read as described.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Case 1 counts vault reads (red today), cases 3/6/7 pin the triggers that are not the tier and name their negative controls, and case 8 guards the tick.
verdicts.builder_notes: No IPC change, but it is a Rust change; §40.6 froze Rust only on the rebuild branch. The dirty-flag inventory is wider than the card lists: vault-only writes (the credential/channel3/key configuration commands change settings with no ledger write), Message::AttachMcp, Action::HouseStatus (in-memory house_state, dispatcher.rs:305), and the approval lock expiring with time (the tick covers this one). Each missed trigger is at most 1 s late. Pin the vault-write case with a test, or set publish_dirty on every vault write. Record write_count after the pass, because record_snapshot_rungs writes. dispatcher admit() refusal calls record_refusal; if that writes, a refused read will publish (correct, but keep it out of case 1). Ledger::write_count is a new public accessor over total_changes; keep it a u64 with no SQL surface.
